facts.text: Latin malefactum, 'an evil deed'; English malefactor, 'evildoer'. The name as the Academy's for him, not the ogres'.

Malefact as the queen's way-finder, the marks he draws because the ogres cannot read the hall-folk's words, the storm-keeper's key broken into pieces along the way, the churls at the door and Master Xavier's name for the storm-keeper are Living Server writing.

story:
Krondon was built by the hall-folk, and the hall-folk built it to be lived in by people who knew the way. Its passages turn and turn back, its doors are carved with words in the old tongue telling where each one goes, and the thrawn ogres who took the hall in Morgana's war could not read one of them. The ghost of Wynflaed, the hall-folk's last teacher, translates their titles for Orylle; it has never translated the doors. So the queen needed someone who could find the way, and the ogres found him among themselves, an ogre of her own household who could not read either but could remember, and draw what he remembered.

The Academy calls him Malefact. It is not his name. Master Xavier of Caer Diogel, who has been trying to get into the hall for years, gave him the word out of an old law-book because he needed something to write in his reports, and the word stuck. What the ogres call him, the hall-folk's ghosts say, is a word that means the one who goes first. He keeps the door, near the entrance, among the churls who thresh and carry there; they are not the queen's own and he is, and he stands among them as a steward stands among the hands. He lets a stranger come close before he looks up. Then he does not stop.

He carries the way. Every turning from the door to the storm-keeper's chamber he has drawn, in marks the ogres made up because they had no letters, on a hide he keeps on him: left after the door, straight, right, the first left, and so on to the worked stone and the end of the passage and the chamber where the four lights burn. The storm-keeper's bargain with the queen was his storm for his hall, and the queen did not trust it; she had the key to his chamber broken and its pieces hidden one at each turning of Malefact's way, so that nobody who did not have the way could ever put it together. Only Malefact knows where every piece lies. He has never needed to use them. The storm-keeper has never tried to leave.

The bundle of ogre-copied curses at Caer Gothwaite has a drawn ogre hand on its last leaf, the first writing any ogre of Krondon ever made. Wenna of Caer Gothwaite believed it was Malefact's. Master Xavier believes the orb that the realm's young bring back from the storm-keeper's chamber is a weapon against the shamans of Midgard. Malefact believes nothing anyone knows of. When he is killed and his hide taken, the door has another one who goes first before long, with another hide, and the same marks on it.
legend: Malefact is a level 50 thrawn ogre of Orylle's own household standing among the ogre ceorls near Krondon's entrance. He is aggressive but only notices you inside about 150, so you can walk quite close. The ceorls round him (46 to 53) are another faction and do not attack on sight; clear the closest ones anyway, since the data does not say whether they would join him. No spells or styles: a melee kill for a small group of fifties. He drops the map for Ogre's Might (Master Xavier in Caer Diogel): follow his directions through Krondon, take a key piece at each turning, and the trail ends at Scurceol Hyrde, the storm-keeper, whose four lights you deal with first. Malefact respawns in about five minutes.

loremasterTopic.text: The thrawn ogre of [orylle]'s own household who keeps the door of [krondon] among the churls and carries the queen's way to the storm-keeper's chamber, drawn on a hide in marks the ogres made up because they could not read the hall-folk's doors. The key to the chamber of the [storm-keeper] was broken and its pieces hidden at each turning of his way. The Academy calls him Malefact; the ogres call him the one who goes first.

bookPage: From the reports of Master Xavier of Caer Diogel to the Academy. The ogre at the door, whom I have called Malefact in these reports for want of anything better, carries a hide with marks on it. I had one brought to me. The marks are not letters. They are the way: a stroke bent left for left, a straight stroke for straight, a ring for the worked stone. At each bend there is a small cut, and at each small cut, my young friends tell me, there lies a piece of a key. I believe it is the key to the chamber of the one the hall-folk called the storm-keeper. I have called him the star channeler in my reports, for the lights. I may have been wrong about that too.
